First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{\pi }^{7\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+y)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+y)]}_{\pi }^{7\pi /6}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{3}+y)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi +y))\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{3}+y)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi +y))\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{3}+y)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi +y)]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{3}+0)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi +\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi +0)] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{17\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{3})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}+0-1] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
